words: first; then; at the end; yesterday; today; we went
cross_subject: ela:ek-discussion (class discussion rules and turns); ela:ek-describe-aloud (telling and describing aloud)
notes: Students tell a partner about a class event (the morning walk, a class visitor) in two pictured steps, then listen and say back one thing the partner did. Entry points (all tell a partner about one class event in two steps and say back one thing the partner told): levels 1 and 2 with two photo cards of the event to point to, a picture word bank and the cloze "First we ___. Then we ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with the photo cards and "First ___. Then ___. It was ___.", taken off before the end-of-unit telling; 5 and 6 with the photo cards only, adding a feeling word, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a two-step telling that opens with "Today we"; past tense of common verbs (went, saw, made) joined with "and then"; the time words first, then, yesterday and today. Model: story map at the K to 1 stage, three pictures in a row; in kindergarten students fill two. Home language: a partner who shares the student's home language may rehearse the telling with them in it first, then both tell it in English; no student translates for another. Carried, owned in grade 3. In kindergarten a telling is two pictured steps about something the whole class saw, so no one needs home or family details; by grade 3, the owner year, the photo cards are gone for levels 3 and 4. Builds on nothing earlier. Teacher note: prompts follow APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground; a home, family or where-you-are-from prompt is one of several, and an invented character or a chosen place is always allowed.

words: this is; it has; we use it to; color; big; small
cross_subject: ela:ek-discussion (class discussion rules and turns); ela:ek-describe-aloud (telling and describing aloud)
notes: Students name and describe a classroom object or a center routine to a partner (what it is, its color, what we use it for) and follow a one-step direction. Entry points (all describe one classroom object so a partner can find it, then follow one direction back): levels 1 and 2 with the real object to hold, a picture word bank of colors and sizes and the cloze "This is a ___. It is ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "This is ___. It has ___. We use it to ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the object hidden in a bag so the words must carry it, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a describing turn that names the thing first and then tells about it; "This is / it has / we use it to"; color and size words and picture labels. Model: text map at the K to 1 stage, the topic as a picture with two facts beside it. Home language: students may name the object in the home language first and then in English; the teacher points out a cognate where one exists (color is spelled the same in Spanish and English). Carried, owned in grade 3. In kindergarten describing stays with things on the table, which every student can see and point to; by grade 3 the object is not in the room. Builds on nothing earlier.

words: how; why; because; so; first; wash
notes: Students say how to do a class job (washing hands, cleaning up blocks) and why we do it, acting out the steps with a partner. Entry points (all act out a class job with a partner and say how to do it and why): levels 1 and 2 with photo step cards to act out, a picture word bank and the cloze "First ___. Then ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with the step cards and "First ___, then ___, because ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the step cards only, joining two reasons with "and" and "so", the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a how-to in two or three steps with the reason last; "When we ___, ___" and "because"; how, why and so. Model: cause chain at the K to 1 stage, two linked boxes (what we do, what happens). Home language: partners may act out and talk through the steps in the home language first; the actions carry the meaning, so no one has to translate. Carried, owned in grade 3. In kindergarten each job has two or three steps the class does every day, so the language rides on a routine students already know; by grade 3 the steps are a problem the group solved, not a routine. Builds on nothing earlier.

words: I think; I like; because; agree; disagree; vote
cross_subject: ela:ek-discussion (class discussion rules and turns); ela:ek-opinion (opinion with a reason, no ELD-LA Argue id before 4-5)
notes: Students say which book, game or picture they like and why, vote, and hear that others chose differently. Entry points (all choose between two books or games, give a reason, vote and hear a different choice): levels 1 and 2 with both choices pictured on the vote chart, a picture word bank of reasons (fun, funny, pretty) and the cloze "I like ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "I think ___ because ___." and "I agree" or "I disagree" cards, off before the end-of-unit vote; 5 and 6 with the vote chart only, giving two reasons and answering a friend who chose the other, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a turn that gives the choice and then the reason; "I think ___ because ___" and "I agree with ___ because"; like, best and favorite. Model: claim chart at the K to 1 stage, a picture vote chart with the choice and one reason. Home language: a student may give the reason in the home language first and the teacher then models it in English to say back; a reason in any language counts as a reason. Carried, owned in grade 3. In kindergarten the choices are two things in the room, and the vote shows that people can choose differently; by grade 3 the group must reach one decision together. Builds on nothing earlier.

words: story; character; first; next; at the end; happy; sad
cross_subject: ela:ek-narrate (narrative writing); ela:ek-retell (reading literature, same text)
notes: Students hear the ELA unit's read-aloud story again and take apart its opening and its ending: who the character is, and the time words that move the story on. They retell it in three parts on a story map with a partner, then tell their own short story with a character, with the teacher first and then with a partner. Reading the story and writing about it stay in ELA. Entry points (all retell the read-aloud in three parts and tell an own story with a character): levels 1 and 2 with three picture cards to order, a picture word bank and the cloze "First ___. Next ___. At the end ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with the story map and "First ___. Next ___. At the end ___. The character felt ___.", off before the end-of-unit telling; 5 and 6 with the story map only, adding a feeling word and a "because" to one part, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a story in three parts (first, next, at the end); past tense of common verbs (ran, saw, said) and "and then"; the time words first, next and at the end, and feeling words happy and sad. Model: story map at the K to 1 stage, three pictures in a row. Home language: a student may tell their own story in the home language first, to a partner who shares it or to a family member at home, then tell it in English; a story in any language is a story. Owner year for LA K. The K expectations in both modes: retelling a heard story and telling one in order. Builds on nothing earlier. Teacher note: prompts follow APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground; a home, family or where-you-are-from prompt is one of several, and an invented character or a chosen place is always allowed.

words: topic; fact; it has; it can; label
cross_subject: ela:ek-inform (informative writing); ela:ek-main-topic (reading informational, same text); ela:ek-sentences (forms of English)
notes: Students hear an information book from the ELA unit again and take apart one page: the topic word and how the page tells two facts about it ("It has", "It can"). They say the topic and two facts, then draw and label their own all-about page with the teacher first and then alone. The reading and writing lessons stay in ELA. Entry points (all say an information book's topic and two facts and make a labeled all-about page): levels 1 and 2 with the book's pictures to point to, a picture word bank and the cloze "It is about ___. It has ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with the text map and "This book is about ___. It has ___. It can ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the text map only, telling a fact the picture does not show, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a page with a topic and two facts; "It is / it has / it can"; labels and the words topic and fact. Model: text map at the K to 1 stage, the topic and its facts. Home language: a student may label the page in the home language beside English if they choose; the teacher names cognates in the book's topic words (animal and animal, planeta and planet). Owner year for LA K. The K expectations in both modes: topic and facts heard and told. Builds on nothing earlier.

words: more; fewer; same; circle; triangle; side; corner
notes: Students describe and compare groups and shapes from the math unit (more, fewer, the same; sides and corners) and tell a partner how they sorted a set. Entry points (all describe and compare groups and shapes from the math unit and tell a partner how they sorted a set): levels 1 and 2 with the real objects to sort and point to, a picture word bank and the cloze "This has ___. It is a ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "This has ___ sides and ___ corners." and "___ has more than ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the shapes hidden behind a folder, describing one so a partner can find it, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a describing turn that names the group or shape and then tells about it; "This has / it is / there are more"; number and shape words, more, fewer and the same. Model: text map at the K to 1 stage, the topic (a shape or group) and two facts. Home language: a student may count and name shapes in the home language first; círculo and circle, triángulo and triangle are cognates. Owner year for MA K. The K expectations in both modes: hearing and giving descriptions of numbers and shapes. Builds on nothing earlier.

words: plant; animal; need; water; food; sunny; rainy; windy
notes: Students describe what plants and animals need and what the weather is each day in the science unit, and keep a picture weather chart they talk through. Entry points (all describe what a plant or animal needs and what the weather is today, from the class weather chart): levels 1 and 2 with picture cards to match, the picture weather chart, a word bank and the cloze "It is ___ today. A plant needs ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "Today it is ___. Yesterday it was ___. ___ needs ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the chart only, comparing two days or two living things, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a short report on today's weather or a living thing's needs; "It is / it needs / they have"; weather words and labels on the chart. Model: text map at the K to 1 stage, the topic and its facts. Home language: a student may name the weather in the home language first; planta and plant, animal and animal are cognates. Owner year for SC K. The K expectations in both modes: hearing and giving descriptions of living things and weather. Builds on nothing earlier.

words: push; pull; fast; slow; harder; warm; because
notes: Students say what happens when they push or pull harder and why the sun warms a surface, after testing it in the science unit. Entry points (all say what happens when they push or pull harder and why the sun warms a surface, after testing it): levels 1 and 2 with the test to act out again, photo cards, a word bank and the cloze "I pushed ___. It went ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "When I push harder, it ___." and "The sun makes it ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the photo cards only, saying what happened and why with "because", the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a short explanation, what we did and what happened; "When ___, ___" and "because"; push, pull, fast and slow. Model: cause chain at the K to 1 stage, two linked boxes (what we did, what happened). Home language: a student may say what happened in the home language first while acting it out; rápido and rapid are cognates, and the teacher pairs rapid with fast. Owner year for SC K. The K expectations in both modes, all parts: hearing and saying the question the class tested or the problem it tried to solve ("What if we push harder?", "How can we keep the slide cool?"), using what was seen to say how or why it happened, telling what was seen, linking what we did to what happened, and comparing two ways the class tried (one hand or two; shade from a tree or from a sheet) to say which worked better, all from the host's own records. Builds on nothing earlier.

words: helper; job; works at; helps; goods; community
notes: Students describe community helpers and their jobs and goods and services from the social studies unit, and tell a partner what one helper does. Entry points (all describe community helpers and their jobs, and goods and services, from the unit's pictures, and tell a partner what one helper does): levels 1 and 2 with the unit's helper pictures, a picture word bank and the cloze "This is a ___. A ___ helps ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "A ___ works at ___. A ___ helps people ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the pictures only, telling how two jobs are alike or different, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a describing turn that names the helper and then tells what they do; "This is / works at / helps"; job and place words and labels. Model: text map at the K to 1 stage, the topic (a helper) and two facts. Home language: a student may name a helper in the home language first; doctor and doctor, policía and police are cognates. Owner year for SS K. The K expectations in both modes: hearing and giving descriptions of people and work. Builds on nothing earlier. Teacher note: no task asks what a family member does for work; students describe helpers from the unit's pictures, visitors and class jobs.

words: then; yesterday; next; last; we went; I saw
cross_subject: ela:e1-discussion (class discussion rules and turns); ela:e1-describe-present (telling and describing aloud)
notes: Students tell a partner about a class event in three parts with time words and listen to a partner tell theirs, asking one "what happened next?" question. Entry points (all tell a class event in three parts and ask a partner "what happened next?"): levels 1 and 2 with three photo cards, the picture word bank and the cloze "First ___. Next ___. At the end ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with the cards and "First ___. Next ___. At the end ___. I felt ___.", off before the end-of-unit telling; 5 and 6 with the cards turned over after one look, adding who was there, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a three-part telling with a beginning, a middle and an end; past tense of common verbs (went, saw, ate, played) and "and then"; first, next, last and yesterday. Home language: a student may rehearse the telling in the home language with a partner who shares it before telling it in English; the partner is never asked to translate. Carried, owned in grade 3. In grade 1 the telling grows from two steps to three and gains a question back, so the listener has a job too; the two-step cloze of kindergarten is gone for levels 3 and 4. Teacher note: prompts follow APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground; a home, family or where-you-are-from prompt is one of several, and an invented character or a chosen place is always allowed.

words: first; then; get; put; next to; line up
cross_subject: ela:e1-discussion (class discussion rules and turns); ela:e1-describe-present (telling and describing aloud)
notes: Students give a partner a two-step direction for a class routine (getting materials, lining up) and follow one back. Entry points (all give a partner a two-step direction for a class routine and follow one back): levels 1 and 2 with photo cards of the two steps, gestures, a picture word bank and the cloze "First get the ___. Then ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "First ___. Then ___. Put it ___." and place words on cards, off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with no cards, checking the partner understood ("Show me"), the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a direction in order, the action word first; commands (get, put, line up) and "This is / it goes"; place words (on, under, next to) and labels. Home language: partners who share a home language may try the direction in it once, then give it in English; gestures and pictures carry the meaning for a student with no partner who shares it. Carried, owned in grade 3. In grade 1 the routine has two steps and a partner checks it back; the kindergarten object is gone, so the words must carry the action.

words: why; because; so; rule; it helps; turn
notes: Students explain how a class game or center works step by step, and why a rule helps. Entry points (all explain how a class game or center works, step by step, and why one rule helps): levels 1 and 2 with photo step cards, a picture word bank and the cloze "First ___. Then ___. The rule helps because ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with step cards and "First ___, then ___, so ___." for the rule, off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the cards only, giving two reasons for the rule and answering a partner's "why?", the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a how-it-works talk that gives the steps and then the reason for a rule; "when ___, ___" and "because" joining a rule to what it stops; why, so and rule. Home language: students may talk through the game in the home language with a partner first; the teacher points out cognates in game words where they exist (Spanish regla and English rule share a root but look different, so the picture card carries it). Carried, owned in grade 3. In grade 1 the steps become a game with a rule, and the reason is for the rule, not the step; the kindergarten act-out is gone for levels 3 and 4.

words: I think; because; I agree with; I disagree; my reason; choose
cross_subject: ela:e1-discussion (class discussion rules and turns); ela:e1-opinion (opinion with a reason, no ELD-LA Argue id before 4-5)
notes: Students give an opinion on a class choice with a reason and say "I agree" or "I disagree" with a partner. Entry points (all give an opinion on a class choice with a reason and say "I agree" or "I disagree" with a partner): levels 1 and 2 with the choices pictured on the vote chart, a picture word bank of reasons and the cloze "I think ___ because ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "I agree with ___ because ___." and "I disagree because ___.", off before the end-of-unit vote; 5 and 6 with the vote chart only, giving two reasons and answering a partner who disagrees, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a turn that states the choice, gives a reason and answers a partner; "I think ___ because" and "I agree with ___ because"; agree, disagree and because. Home language: a student may think the reason through in the home language and say it in English with the frame; the teacher welcomes a reason said first in the home language. Carried, owned in grade 3. In grade 1 the opinion meets a partner's opinion, so agreeing and disagreeing join the telling; the kindergarten "I like" cloze is gone for levels 3 and 4.

words: character; setting; lesson; then; in the end; learned
cross_subject: ela:e1-narrative (narrative writing); ela:e1-retell-lesson (reading literature, same text)
notes: Students take apart the ELA unit story's last page: how the writer shows the lesson and closes the story. They retell the story with its character, setting and lesson, then build a two- or three-event story with time words and a closing line, with the teacher first and then alone. The full story writing stays in ELA. Entry points (all retell the ELA story with its lesson and tell and write a short story with a closing): levels 1 and 2 with picture cards to sequence, a picture word bank and the cloze "The story is about ___. The lesson is ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with the story map and "First ___. Then ___. In the end ___ learned ___.", off before the end-of-unit writing task; 5 and 6 with the story map only, adding a detail to each event and a closing line of their own, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a story with a beginning, events and a closing that gives the lesson; past tense of common verbs and "and then"; time words (first, then, in the end) and the words setting and lesson. Model: story map at the K to 1 stage, three pictures, now with a closing box for the lesson. Home language: a student may plan the story in the home language first; many folk tales the class reads have versions in other languages, and a family may share one at home by choice. Owner year for LA 1. Both modes at grade 1: a retold story with its lesson and an own story with an ending. Teacher note: prompts follow APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground; a home, family or where-you-are-from prompt is one of several, and an invented character or a chosen place is always allowed.

words: topic; heading; caption; they can; now you know; closing
cross_subject: ela:e1-informative (informative writing); ela:e1-main-topic (reading informational, same text); ela:e1-sentences (forms of English)
notes: Students take apart one page of the ELA unit text: how a heading names the topic and a caption tells a fact. They find the main topic and facts, then build a fact page with a closing sentence, with the teacher first and then alone. The reading lessons on text features stay in ELA. Entry points (all find an ELA text's topic and facts from its headings and captions and write a fact page with a closing): levels 1 and 2 with the text's pictures and headings to point to, a picture word bank and the cloze "This is about ___. It has ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with the text map and "___ are ___. They can ___. Now you know about ___.", off before the end-of-unit writing task; 5 and 6 with the text map only, adding a fact from a caption and a closing of their own, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a fact page with a topic, facts and a closing sentence; "This is / it has / they can"; heading, caption, label and the closing "Now you know". Model: text map at the K to 1 stage, topic and facts, with a closing line added. Home language: a student may write the caption in the home language beside English if they choose; the teacher names cognates in heading words. Owner year for LA 1. Both modes at grade 1: text features read and a fact page with a closing written.

words: sides; corners; most; least; how many more; chart
cross_subject: math:m1-shape-attributes (shape attributes); math:m1-data-three-categories (reading a data chart)
notes: Students describe shapes by their attributes and tell what a three-category data chart shows (most, least, how many more) from the math unit. Entry points (all describe shapes by their attributes and tell what a three-category data chart shows): levels 1 and 2 with the shapes and the chart to point to, a picture word bank and the cloze "It has ___ sides. ___ has the most.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "A ___ has ___. ___ has ___ more than ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the chart and shapes out of sight, telling a partner how to sort or compare, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a description of a shape or a chart, the topic first and then the facts; "has / has more than / has the most"; side, corner, most and least. Model: text map at the K to 1 stage, topic and facts, with a fact from a chart. Home language: a student may count and compare in the home language first; the teacher names cognates in data words (categoría and category). Owner year for MA 1. Both modes at grade 1: describing attributes and data heard and told.

words: parent; young; signal; protect; alike; pattern; sunrise; sunset
cross_subject: science:s1-parent-offspring (host investigation); science:s1-like-parents (host investigation, earlier); science:s1-sky-patterns (host investigation)
notes: Students describe a pattern of behavior from the science unit that runs alongside, how young animals signal (crying, cheeping, an open mouth) and how their parents respond (feeding, protecting), and the patterns of the sun and moon; how young animals and plants are like their parents is retrieved from the earlier science unit, which comes first in the host order. Entry points (all describe how a young animal signals and its parent responds, and a pattern of the sun or moon): levels 1 and 2 with matching picture cards (a signal and its response, sky pictures), a word bank and the cloze "When the baby ___, the parent ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "When the young ___ ___, the parent ___. This helps the young ___." and a pattern frame ("Every day the sun ___."), off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the cards only, adding how the young is like and not like its parent, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a short report on a pattern of behavior or of the sky; "When ___, ___", "every day" and, retrieved, "Both ___ have"; signal, protect, pattern and alike. Model: text map at the K to 1 stage, the topic and its facts, now grouped into alike and different. Home language: a student may name the animals in the home language first; the teacher names cognates in animal names where they exist (elefante and elephant). Owner year for SC 1. Both modes at grade 1: describing patterns and likenesses. Teacher note: the lesson stays with animals and plants and never turns to "How are you like your parents?"; some students live apart from a parent, in foster care or with an adoptive family.

words: sound; vibrate; light; dark; shadow; because
notes: Students explain that sound comes from vibration and that we see when there is light, after investigating in the science unit. Entry points (all explain that sound comes from vibration and that we see when there is light, after investigating): levels 1 and 2 with the investigation to show again (a drum, a box with a peephole), a word bank and the cloze "It vibrates. It makes ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "It makes sound because ___." and "We can see it when ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the cause chain only, joining an observation to a reason in their own sentence, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: an explanation from what we saw to why; "when ___, ___" and "because"; vibrate, light, dark and shadow. Model: cause chain at the K to 1 stage, two linked boxes. Home language: a student may explain in the home language first while showing the test; vibrar and vibrate are cognates. Owner year for SC 1. Both modes at grade 1, all parts: saying the question the class tested or the problem it tried to solve, putting several observations together to say why, picking the observation that supports a point in an explanation, telling what was seen, linking events to what happened, and comparing two ways the class tried (two ways to make the drum louder; opening the flap or shining a flashlight through a hole) to say which worked better, all from the host's own records.

words: mountain; river; lake; leader; the job is to; group
notes: Students describe landforms and bodies of water and the roles in a group from the social studies unit. Entry points (all describe a landform or body of water and the roles in a group, from the unit): levels 1 and 2 with pictures of landforms and role cards, a word bank and the cloze "This is a ___. It has ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "A ___ is ___. The leader's job is to ___.", off before the end-of-unit task; 5 and 6 with the pictures only, comparing two places or two roles, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a description of a place or a role, the topic first and then the facts; "This is / it has / the job is to"; landform words and group-role words. Model: text map at the K to 1 stage, topic and facts, grouped into places and roles. Home language: a student may name landforms in the home language first; montaña and mountain, lago and lake are cognates. Owner year for SS 1. Both modes at grade 1: describing places and roles.

words: I think; reason; vote; choose; problem; should
notes: Students give a claim with reasons about a class or community problem and vote, from the social studies unit. Entry points (all give a claim with reasons about a class or community problem and vote): levels 1 and 2 with the problem pictured on the vote chart, a picture word bank and the cloze "I think we should ___ because ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "I think ___ because ___. I vote for ___.", off before the end-of-unit vote; 5 and 6 with the claim chart only, giving two reasons and answering a classmate's choice, the frame gone after the first application day; the kindergarten text map of facts is faded here into the claim chart. Forms: a claim with reasons and a vote; "I think ___ because" and "should"; vote, choose and problem. Model: claim chart at the K to 1 stage, a picture vote chart with the choice and one reason. Home language: a student may give the reason in the home language first; votar and vote, problema and problem are cognates. Owner year for SS 1. Both modes at grade 1, all parts: naming the topic of a claim, finding what a short pictured source about the problem says (a class survey chart or a note from the office, Curio Class's own, invented for practice), telling a fact that can be checked from an opinion ("The bench is broken" or "Blue is the best color"), choosing the fact that supports the claim and saying how it supports it with "because" or "so". Builds on kindergarten SI Argue and kindergarten SS Inform, since ELD-SS has no Argue id in K.

words: after that; finally; we went; my partner said; later; it was
cross_subject: ela:e2-discussion (class discussion rules and turns); ela:e2-tell-and-record (telling and describing aloud)
notes: Students recount a class event or a school trip in order with details, then retell a partner's recount to a third student. Entry points (all recount a class event or school trip in order with details, then retell a partner's recount to a third student): levels 1 and 2 with photo cards of the event, the picture word bank and the cloze "First ___. After that ___. Finally ___.", the cloze off before the check and the word bank kept; 3 and 4 with "First ___. After that ___. Finally ___. My partner said ___.", off before the end-of-unit telling; 5 and 6 with the cards only, adding a detail and a feeling and choosing what the third student needs to know, the frame gone after the first application day. Forms: a recount with an opening that says when and where; irregular past verbs (went, saw, ate, took) and "My partner said that"; then, after that and finally. Home language: partners who share a home language may plan the recount in it first; Spanish cognates for trip words (museo and museum, autobús and bus) go on the word cards. Carried, owned in grade 3. In grade 2 students add details and retell a partner's recount without the teacher leading every turn; in grade 3, the owner year, the photo cards are gone for levels 3 and 4. Teacher note: prompts follow APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground; a home, family or where-you-are-from prompt is one of several, and an invented character or a chosen place is always allowed.
